note: Logging surface beyond the core set in 30-logging.json.

assertions.claim: LoggingOptions is a `{RootNamespace}.Core.Configuration` type — that is the using the sample needs.
RequestOptions is a `{RootNamespace}.Core` type — the per-call options live under .Core, NOT under .Core.Configuration where LoggingOptions lives.
assertions.defends: dotnet-calling-endpoints § requestOptions; dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, per-call override

assertions.claim: `Logging` is a real, settable property on the options class, defaulted to `new()` — which is what makes `options.Logging = new LoggingOptions { ... }` compile and `options.Logging.X` safe to read. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
assertions.defends: dotnet-client-initialization § options class; dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, the options sample

assertions.claim: No LoggingOptions member is `required`, so the skill's object initializer — which sets only four of the ten — compiles as written.
LoggerFactory is a nullable ILoggerFactory with no default — 'you leave LoggerFactory null' is the state the three-state table is about.
LogRequestHeaders, LogResponseHeaders and LogRequestBody are all bools with no initializer, i.e. all three default to false.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, the options sample and the 'On by default' column

assertions.claim: The masked replacement is RedactionPlaceholder, defaulting to "***".
The SDK logs under the category '{client type name}.Http' — the string a host's log filters must target.

The client hands the logger its own type name, so the log category is '{Api}Client.Http' and the environment variable is '{APICLIENTTYPENAME}_LOG' for that same name. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
A hand-built client with no LoggerFactory (and no environment variable) gets NullLoggerFactory — nothing is written.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, the three-state table, row 2

assertions.claim: The request and success-response lines are Information and on by default — no option has to be set to get them.
The three payload rows are opt-in and emit below Information: headers at Debug, body at Trace, each gated by its own switch rather than on by default.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, the event table's 'On by default' column

assertions.claim: The response line is Information on success and Warning on failure — the level is chosen per response, not fixed in the LoggerMessage attribute.
A terminal failure is logged at Error with the exception attached to the record, not just formatted into the message.
The environment variable accepts exactly info, debug or trace — trimmed and lower-cased, and anything else (information, warn, 1) is silently ignored.
`debug` additionally forces request AND response headers on — and only trace, not debug, forces the body on.

Every accepted value installs the built-in console logger as the factory — that is how the variable gets output to stderr with no code change. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.
RedactedHeaders forces a header in and UnmaskHeaders opts one out — tested in that order, so UnmaskHeaders wins when a header is in both.
RedactedKeys ADDS to the masked set: it is ORed in front of the allow-list test, so its keys are masked in a form body as well as in a query string.
The URL path is NOT masked — it is concatenated into the logged URL as-is, so an id or reference in the route is logged verbatim; only the query goes through MaskPairs.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, 'The URL path is not masked'

assertions.claim: The built-in logger is on the request hot path — RawClient opens a log scope for the call and reports the outgoing request from inside the attempt, so you do not need a DelegatingHandler to see requests.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, opening line; dotnet-client-initialization § options class

assertions.claim: requestOptions is a per-call LOGGING override and nothing else: exactly one place in Core reads a member off it, and that place is the HTTP logger.
